Kodiak AI, Inc. (Nasdaq: KDK), founded in 2018, is a leader in Physical AI, developing driverless technology that powers machines that move. Its Kodiak Driver is a vehicle-agnostic autonomous driving system that combines AI-powered software with modular hardware. Today it operates in long-haul trucking, industrial trucking, and defense. In this role, you will:
Develop test plans and create simulations to test the behavior of autonomous trucks.
Run daily simulation operations, including scenario execution, triage, and reporting.
Improve efficiency in test planning, scenario execution, and results tracking across large-scale simulation suites.
Partner with engineering teams to ensure simulation scenarios accurately reflect real-world conditions.
Work closely with systems engineers on structured test design and execution, ensuring comprehensive coverage of safety-critical and edge-case scenarios.
Share actionable insights from simulation results with autonomy software engineers to accelerate software development and validation.
Collaborate with infrastructure and tools teams to enhance automation, debugging, and scaling of simulations.
Support manufacturing through DFM/DFA reviews, supplier qualification, First Article Inspection, prototype builds, production launches, and field engineering activities.
Qualifications:
Master of Science degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Data Science, or a closely related field.

Testing and creating simulation scenarios in Applied Intuition simulation environment to validate end-to-end autonomous vehicle (AV) software interaction features with fleet management web service software.
AV hardware configurations, including LiDAR, radar, and camera-based sensor technologies.
Developing detailed test plans with traceability to user requirements.
Executing structured test runs on an actual vehicle to verify AV software stack module features.
Analyzing test results and vehicle logs across perception, planning, localization, controls and other system-level behaviors as part of the triage and root cause process.
